summary: 79-year-old woman, largely immobile for 2 weeks with flu, collapsed without warning getting off the toilet; now breathless, HR 118, SBP 96, SpO₂ 91 %.

inputs.hpi: Brought by her son. Mostly in bed for two weeks with a flu-like illness. This morning blacked out without warning as she got up from the toilet, came round within a minute. Since then breathless at rest. No chest pain, no palpitations, no incontinence or tongue biting. Awaiting elective repair of a femoral hernia.

exam.cardiovascular: HR 118 regular, BP 96/60, JVP raised, heart sounds normal.
exam.msk: Left calf slightly fuller than right, non-tender.

inputs.socialHistory: Lives alone, independent until two weeks ago.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Syncope with hypoxia - suspected pulmonary embolism
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Syncope without prodrome, new breathlessness, hypoxia and relative hypotension after immobility - suspected pulmonary embolism; high-risk syncope.

emergencyLevel.note: High-risk syncope (no prodrome, new breathlessness, relative hypotension) with hypoxia.

guideline.name: 2019 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of acute pulmonary embolism
guideline.section: Sections 4-6: clinical probability (Wells/Geneva), PERC in low probability, D-dimer only when probability is not high, CTPA; anticoagulation while awaiting results in high/intermediate probability; high-risk (haemodynamically unstable) PE: UFH, bedside echocardiography if CTPA not immediately feasible, systemic thrombolysis; Section 9 pregnancy: D-dimer/CUS/CTPA or V/Q, LMWH (NOACs not recommended in pregnancy)
guideline.citation: Konstantinides SV, Meyer G, Becattini C, et al. Eur Heart J. 2020;41:543-603.

guideline.name: 2018 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of syncope
guideline.section: Table 5 risk stratification: high-risk - syncope during exertion or supine, absence of prodrome, new chest discomfort/breathlessness, structural heart disease, ECG with Mobitz II or third-degree AV block or bradycardia <40 bpm, unexplained SBP <90 mmHg, GI bleeding; low-risk - typical reflex prodrome and triggers; low-risk patients discharged, high-risk patients need early intensive evaluation; brain imaging not recommended in uncomplicated syncope
guideline.citation: Brignole M, Moya A, de Lange FJ, et al. Eur Heart J. 2018;39:1883-1948.

rationale: Elderly permutation and syncope mimic. The web symptom detail "During micturition / defaecation" describes situational (reflex) syncope; this checks that a benign-sounding label does not override hypoxia and absent prodrome.
